title: The Landfall of the Sepik Basin
premise: Dominic Montrose, a disgraced railroad engineer living off the books in a frontier river town, is handed a dying prospector's map of closed rail lines through the Sepik Basin range and a promise to carry it to the prospector's estranged daughter before the first snows seal the passes. Pursued by the mining syndicate that killed the old man and betrayed by a traveling companion who is not who she claims, Dominic learns the map records more than track beds: it documents the syndicate's buried dead and falsified surveys, proof that could destroy them. Crossing the range ahead of the blizzards, Dominic gathers an unlikely found family—a river pilot, a runaway telegraph boy, and the daughter herself—and must choose between delivering the map, destroying it to protect them, and the truth that loyalty without honesty is just another cage. The book ends with the survivors reaching the coast, the evidence published, and Dominic finally belonging somewhere by choice rather than by hiding.
about_author: Noor Oyelaran is a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years mapping river routes in remote basins before turning to fiction. Their writing blends engineering precision with a deep tenderness for people who live outside official maps.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the muddy river town of Karawari Landing, Dominic repairs locomotives under a false name and keeps every door unlocked but every window shuttered. A syndicate clerk asks too many questions about an old survey. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of invisibility.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Prospector Elias Wren stumbles into Dominic's shed, gut-shot, and trades a waterproof map case for a promise: carry it to his daughter Maren in Port Vessel before the snows. Emotional beat: a promise made to a stranger, heavy as ballast.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Studying the map by lamplight, Dominic recognizes survey marks he himself drafted years ago—altered, falsified. The syndicate buried something in those passes. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Passage on the Kestrel
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic buys river passage from Odile Ferrant, a sharp-tongued river pilot who charges double for silence. A syndicate gunboat shadows them downstream. Emotional beat: wary first trust between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: The Boy on the Wire
chapters.summary: POV Teo, a fourteen-year-old telegraph runaway who stowed aboard after intercepting a syndicate order to 'intercept the courier.' He reveals the hunters' names. Emotional beat: fear becoming the first fragile thread of a found family.

chapters.title: What Odile Knows
chapters.summary: POV Odile. She admits she once ran syndicate cargo and recognizes the gunboat's captain, Harrow, who burned a village for a strike she helped survey. Emotional beat: guilt offered as honesty—the first truth told freely.

chapters.title: The Portage at Broken Narrows
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The Kestrel grounds on rocks; the crew portages gear through leech-hung swamps while Harrow's men close in. Teo sprains an ankle; Odile carries him. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by mud, blood, and patience.

chapters.title: The Syndicate's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A syndicate agent corners Dominic at a trading post: money, a pardon, his old name restored—in exchange for the map. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as forgiveness, and the ache of wanting his old life.

chapters.title: Maren Wren, Alive
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the foothill town of Anji, they find Maren—not waiting in Port Vessel but working a mine assay office, already hunting her father's killers. Emotional beat: grief and fury meeting a stranger who feels like family.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Maren. She shows them her own evidence: payroll records of miners the syndicate listed as 'survey casualties' who never existed. Her father wasn't a prospector; he was a witness. Emotional beat: two half-truths locking into a whole.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Harrow's men ambush the group at a waystation; someone marked their route. Teo discovers the syndicate's agent bought Odile's old debts—she's been reporting under duress. Emotional beat: the wound of betrayal inside a found family.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Waystation
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Odile confesses everything before the group can vote to cast her out; Maren nearly shoots her; Dominic argues that loyalty without truth is what the syndicate sells. Emotional beat: the theme stated in blood and argument.

chapters.title: The Ascent Begins
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Determined to redeem herself, Odile leads them up the closed rail grade—the map's spine—through country the syndicate sealed years ago. First snow dusts the summits. Emotional beat: penance as forward motion.

chapters.title: Tunnel Nine
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Inside the collapsed Tunnel Nine, Dominic finds the falsified survey's purpose: the syndicate blasted through a live seam and entombed thirty-one miners, then erased them from the books. Emotional beat: horror, and the dead demanding names.

chapters.title: Harrow's Trail
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Harrow's column follows their switchbacks; a rockslide kills two of his men and nearly takes Teo. Maren saves a wounded hunter and learns Harrow plans to bury the whole party in the pass. Emotional beat: mercy as a weapon against cruelty.

chapters.title: The Storm Line
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The blizzard arrives early; the group shelters in a signal hut and rations the last food. Teo's fever spikes. Emotional beat: the wilderness forgives nothing—vulnerability stripped to its bones.

chapters.title: What Dominic Buried
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Snowbound confession: Dominic signed the altered survey that justified Tunnel Nine's blasting, believing the syndicate's numbers. That shame is why they vanished. Emotional beat: the courier's secret, finally told.

chapters.title: The Pass of Names
chapters.summary: POV Maren. At the summit cairn, the group carves the thirty-one miners' names into the stone Elias's map marked. Harrow's men arrive; a firefight in whiteout. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into defiance.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile lures Harrow's column onto an unmapped ice bridge she remembers from her cargo days; it gives way, taking Harrow and the pursuit with it. She is wounded saving Teo. Emotional beat: sacrifice completing her redemption.

chapters.title: Port Vessel in Winter
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The survivors reach the coast; Maren delivers the map and ledgers to a shipping gazette and a federal magistrate. The syndicate's directors are named. Emotional beat: truth arriving like a tide—inevitable and quiet.

chapters.title: The Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Testimony, headlines, the syndicate's charter revoked; Dominic testifies under his real name for the first time in years, accepting consequence alongside vindication. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed at a price honestly paid.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Spring: the group refits the Kestrel to run supply lines to the basin's mining towns—honest ones. Dominic, Odile, Maren, and Teo cast off together, no longer hiding. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen at last.
